evidence.detail: R40 SceneTile (rs/H) owns rs/I in its dedicated modeled-tile surface slot, while rs/V Scene constructs rs/I only for tile shapes outside the two simple paint cases and stores it into that slot.

rs/I builds per-tile vertex coordinate arrays and triangle-index/color/texture arrays from fixed shape and rotation tables using the 128-unit tile grid, interpolated corner heights and overlay/underlay colors.
Scene consumes rs/I vertex/face arrays as the non-flat tile geometry representation; the object also exposes shape/rotation metadata and textured-face data.

proposals.note: SceneTileModel is the modern semantic name for the shaped/triangulated per-tile scene geometry object; this is not a claim of verbatim original-source naming.

evidence.detail: R40 SceneTile (rs/H) owns rs/J in its dedicated simple-tile surface slot, and rs/V Scene constructs rs/J for the two simple tile cases before storing it directly into that slot.
rs/J is a compact immutable tile-surface record holding four corner colors, texture/overlay metadata and a flatness flag, with only three auxiliary mutable color fields used by the scene pipeline.
Scene distinguishes rs/J from rs/I: rs/J represents the simple painted tile surface while rs/I represents shaped/triangulated tile geometry.

proposals.note: SceneTilePaint is the modern semantic name for the simple painted per-tile surface object; this is not a claim of verbatim original-source naming.
